title: Hooks: from request to rule
summary: CLAUDE.md asks; a hook makes sure. Hooks are small commands Claude Code runs at fixed moments, every time, so the things that must happen do.

props.text: Hooks are user-defined shell commands. Claude Code runs them at specific points in its lifecycle, which gives you deterministic control: certain actions always happen rather than relying on the LLM to choose to run them.

props.title: See your hooks
props.ask: Explain what hooks are configured in this project, if any.
props.expect: Or type `/hooks` in Claude Code: a read-only list of every hook, when it fires and which file it came from. To add one, ask Claude, then read it before you accept it.

steps.title: A request
steps.text: CLAUDE.md can ask Claude to run the formatter after every edit, and it usually will. But it's a request, like a *please knock* sign: Claude reads it and tries to follow it, with no guarantee.

steps.title: A rule
steps.text: A **hook** is a command Claude Code runs automatically at a set moment, every time. Claude doesn't choose to run it; Claude Code does. That's a door that locks itself, and it's deterministic: same moment, same command.

steps.title: Block
steps.text: Before Claude edits a file, a hook checks the path. For `data/raw` it prints a reason and ends with **exit code 2**: the number a program hands back when it finishes, which for this hook means *stop*. The edit never happens.

m-pre.body: **Block:** exit code 2 stops the edit. `data/raw` stays untouched.

steps.title: Tidy
steps.text: After each edit, a hook runs the formatter (a tool that tidies a file's layout) on that file. Nobody has to remember. It sees only what you point it at: tied to Claude's edit tools, it misses a file changed by a command.

m-post.body: **Tidy:** runs the formatter on the file Claude just edited.

steps.title: Inform
steps.text: When a session starts, a hook can run a command and hand what it prints to Claude. This one searches the notes for `TODO(sam)`, so Claude begins with Sam's open tasks already in its **context window**, everything it can see at once.

m-start.body: **Inform:** adds Sam's open tasks to Claude's context.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: `DEV_VALIDATOR`, from *Codenames*, is a Stop hook. When Claude says it's done, the hook runs the tests and compares the output with a known-good sample. If they differ, exit code 2 sends Claude back to work.

m-stop.body: **Check:** `DEV_VALIDATOR` runs the tests; exit code 2 keeps Claude working.

steps.title: Where they live
steps.text: Hooks are written in a settings file: `.claude/settings.json` for one project, `~/.claude/settings.json` for all of yours. They run with your permissions, so read one before you add it. And a hook runs only what you wrote: a mistyped path quietly does nothing.

steps.title: From request to rule
steps.text: Use CLAUDE.md for guidance and hooks for whatever must happen every time. The hooks are deterministic, Claude is probabilistic: the hybrid uses each for what it's good at.
